newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's ruling PRI loses control of lower house.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's ruling PRI loses control of lower house.

text.p: Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) has lost control of the lower house of Congress for the first time in 68 years in mid-term elections, preliminary results showed on Monday.
With 61 percent of Sunday's votes counted, the PRI had 36.74 percent, well short of 42 percent needed to keep its majority in the Chamber of Deputies under Mexico's electoral rules.
The conservative National Action Party (PAN) won 27.89 percent and the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) had 26.44 percent, the official results showed.
Other smaller parties, led by the upstart Mexican Ecology Green Party (PVEM) with 4.30 percent of votes cast, had the remainder, the preliminary results showed.
The PRI has governed Mexico for 68 years and until Sunday, had lost only a handful of city races and governorships during its long reign.

In the key vote for Mexico City mayor, the PRD's Cuauhtemoc Cardenas had gained 47.7 percent of the vote with more than 56 percent of the vote counted. His nearest challenger, ruling party candidate Alfredo del Mazo, had 25.30 percent.
